status: Private execution contract recorded before evaluation; no live/provider/public/product/owner admission
ownership: A concrete providers/windows inventory_session owns the existing serialized capture coordinator and actual namespace/storage adapters. An immutable publication owns its actual capture graph and matching sealed current/last-complete native frames and identity evidence. Runtime graph/frontend types retain a generic graph input owner only; no Windows evidence dependency in runtime headers.
source_modes: Existing namespace /1 and storage Metadata /1 or IdentityLayout /2 remain. Storage Frame projection is still the default; Identity projection requires the existing /2 profile explicitly. No new reader role, query profile, command or product default. Comparisons remain explicit bounded prior-digest/subject selections, without namespace/storage or physical-hint coalescence.
publication: Reader start/release/poll/cancel/timeout/retire and capture advancement are explicit. Prepare and validate an immutable native publication before swapping its port cell. Every observation node must match an actual retained frame's exact native domain/source/capture/worker/frame/context; identity reference names resolve complete values only through matching native owners. Failure preserves prior publication and leaves the actual newer capture eligible for retry. Duplicate preparation of the same capture view preserves its pointer. Pending/failed/late source states retain matching stale evidence and explicit coverage.
port: A readonly port owns a shared publication cell, exposes the prepared generic graph by an aliasing shared pointer and exposes its corresponding immutable native publication. Cached callbacks return that pointer without polling, launching, waiting, retiring, dispatching native APIs or allocating a rebuild. The port may outlive its session; it retains data, not reader handles or fresh-media authority. The contract remains serialized and admits no concurrent access.
frontend: The existing frontend observation port publishes the supplied graph only after successful validation/allocation. On failure retain snapshot, selection and previously acknowledged pointer, leaving the same prepared publication eligible for retry. Accepted GraphSnapshot objects retain the generic input owner, so held older frontend snapshots keep the native publication alive after newer delivery or session teardown. Direct by-value graph construction retains its existing semantics and supplies no native retrieval ownership.
retrieval: An actual publication resolves a present observation's complete native frame, or an advertised identity reference name, without I/O. Refuse missing nodes, incompatible source/kind, absent names, foreign domain or mismatched binding. Namespace/storage source and epoch distinctions remain exact. A reference hash, copied JSON graph or generic shared pointer alone cannot create native publication ownership, a durable cross-process resolver or a storage grant.
limits: Keep existing source8, namespace64 volumes/mounts, storage16 subjects/128 selected details,16 comparisons, node16KiB/1024values/depth16, graph786432bytes/32768values/320nodes/512edges, display, process/job and worker budgets. Retain bounded current/last-complete frames and required prior comparison values, no publication/projection history chain. Aggregate overflow refuses explicitly without truncation or widening.
checks: Native x64/Win32 mixed actual owned injected namespace/storage readers; exact bindings, complete frame/reference bytes, all retained rows and independent source coverage, without controller storage/namespace API dispatch.
Existing Metadata /1, IdentityLayout /2 Frame and explicit /2 Identity compositions; unchanged defaults, comparisons, duplicate/cloned evidence, names, identifiers and fixed budgets.
